summary: Repeater Item: inside a repeater's item component, exposes this row's item id and its add/remove lifecycle.
description: Repeater Item gives an item component access to its own position in the enclosing Repeater. `itemId` outputs the id of the object this instance renders — the key that lets row-level actions target row-level data. `added` fires when the instance enters the list; `tryRemove` initiates this row's removal, with `removeCompleted` letting an exit animation finish before the instance is destroyed.
whenToUse: Any per-row behaviour in a repeated component: writing back to the row's object, removal buttons, staggered entrance/exit animation. Outside a repeater item component the node has nothing to bind to.

ports.itemId: The id of this row's item object; wire into Object/Set Object Properties `modelId` or bubble it out via Component Outputs.
ports.tryRemove: Signal output firing when removal of this row is requested — run your exit animation, then confirm.
ports.removeCompleted: Signal input; confirms removal after `tryRemove`, letting the repeater delete the instance.

patterns: `itemId` → Set Object Properties `modelId`: row edits write to exactly this row (27 occurrences in the real-project corpus).
